c.tagline: Green city in the sun, safari gateway of East Africa.

taxi.color: no official uniform color; often white or branded
taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis are rare — agree the fare upfront before the ride, or use app-based Uber/Bolt/Little Cab for transparent, prepaid pricing.

emergency.note: 112 works from all mobile networks and routes to police, fire and ambulance; private responders like St. John Ambulance and AAR/Flying Doctors also serve tourists.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: "Nairobbery" — avoid the CBD and River Rd after dark.
Enter the Kibera and Mathare slums only on organised tours; carjacking risk — keep doors locked.

hood_desc: Nairobi's liveliest commercial and nightlife hub, packed with malls, restaurants and international hotels; suits business travelers and visitors who want easy dining and entertainment access.
A leafy, spacious suburb near Nairobi National Park, the Giraffe Centre and Karen Blixen Museum; suits safari-goers and travelers wanting a quiet, green base.
The compact, historic downtown core with markets, government buildings and legacy hotels within walking distance of key sights; suits budget travelers and those needing central transit links.
A business district of glass towers, embassies and conference hotels just south of downtown; suits corporate travelers and conference-goers wanting proximity to the CBD.
A trendy, up-and-coming residential-commercial strip with serviced apartments, cafes and a young professional crowd; suits mid-range travelers wanting a local, walkable feel.
lodging: Best Western Plus Meridian Hotel Nairobi
Four Points by Sheraton Nairobi Hurlingham

water.note: Tap water isn't recommended for tourists despite meeting national standards; stick to bottled water.

transit.pay: Matatus and buses are usually paid in cash to the conductor, though mobile money (M-Pesa) is increasingly accepted; the newer BRT and some Citi Hoppa routes use tap cards. Nairobi Commuter Rail tickets are bought at station counters. Most visitors find ride-hailing apps (Uber, Bolt, Little Cab), paid in-app, far simpler.
transit.hours: Matatus and buses generally run about 5am-10pm with limited late-night service; ride-hailing apps operate 24/7 and are the recommended option after dark.
transit.note: Traffic congestion is severe at peak hours; the matatu system is extensive and inexpensive but chaotic, so many visitors rely on ride-hailing apps for comfort and safety.

train: Madaraka Express (SGR) to Mombasa/Naivasha from Nairobi Terminus

airport.name: Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (NBO)
airport.drive: 30-45 min (up to 90 min in rush-hour traffic)

transit.m: Route 34 'Citi Hoppa' city bus to CBD (~45-60 min)

tip.r: Tipping isn't obligatory but is appreciated; round up or leave 5-10% at restaurants for good service, and tip safari guides/drivers roughly $5-10/day.

food.name: Nyama choma
food.desc: Goat or beef roasted slowly over charcoal, chopped on a board and eaten by hand with kachumbari salad and ugali. The default Kenyan celebration meal.

places.name: Carnivore Restaurant
places.note: The famous open-air grill on Langata Road, roasting meats on Maasai swords since 1980.

places.name: K'Osewe Ranalo Foods
places.note: Packed downtown canteen on Kimathi Lane serving no-frills Kenyan classics at lunch.

places.name: Kenyatta Market
places.note: A whole corridor of charcoal grills where locals pick their cut by weight.

food.name: Ugali with sukuma wiki
food.desc: Stiff white maize meal eaten with braised collard greens and often a stew. The everyday staple plate across Kenya.

places.name: K'Osewe Ranalo Foods
places.note: Go-to lunch spot for ugali with greens, fish or beef stew; arrive before 1pm.

places.name: Amaica Restaurant
places.note: Sit-down restaurant devoted to traditional Kenyan cooking from several regions.

places.name: Kenyatta Market
places.note: Cheap stalls plating ugali and sukuma alongside the grilled meat counters.

food.name: Mutura
food.desc: Kenyan blood sausage: intestine casing stuffed with spiced minced meat and blood, grilled over coals and sliced into coin-sized pieces with chilli.

places.name: Kenyatta Market
places.note: Reliable, busy grills where the mutura turns over quickly; ask for it fresh off the fire.

places.name: Burma Market
places.note: Nairobi's best-known meat market and a classic mutura destination for locals.

places.name: Kirinyaga Road stalls
places.note: Evening street grills near River Road; go with a local and eat where the queue is.

food.name: Samosas and bhajia
food.desc: Crisp triangular meat or vegetable samosas and spiced potato bhajia, the enduring snack legacy of Nairobi's South Asian community.

places.name: Diamond Plaza
places.note: Food court and street stalls in Nairobi's Indian quarter; strong for snacks and chai.

places.name: City Market
places.note: Covered market off Muindi Mbingu Street with snack counters among the produce stalls.

places.name: Kenyatta Market
places.note: Fry stalls turning out samosas and bhajia all day beside the nyama choma grills.

food.name: Fried tilapia with ugali
food.desc: Whole Lake Victoria tilapia deep-fried until crisp and served with ugali and greens, a Luo speciality that Nairobi has adopted wholesale.

places.name: Mama Oliech Restaurant
places.note: The city's most famous fish house on Marcus Garvey Road; whole tilapia is the order.

places.name: K'Osewe Ranalo Foods
places.note: Downtown rival for fried and wet-fried tilapia; loud, fast and cheap.

places.name: Kenyatta Market
places.note: Fish stalls serving smaller tilapia at a fraction of restaurant prices.

food.name: Chapati and mandazi
food.desc: Flaky pan-fried flatbread eaten with beef or bean stew, and mandazi, the lightly sweet cardamom-scented doughnut taken with morning tea.

places.name: Amaica Restaurant
places.note: Traditional menu that pairs chapati with slow-cooked stews rather than rice.

places.name: City Market
places.note: Morning stalls frying mandazi to order for the office crowd.

places.name: K'Osewe Ranalo Foods
places.note: Chapati available alongside ugali as a starch option with any stew.

food.name: Kenyan chai
food.desc: Tea brewed entirely in milk with plenty of sugar, sometimes spiced with cardamom and ginger as masala chai. Kenya grows some of the world's best tea.

places.name: Diamond Plaza
places.note: Masala chai stalls alongside the samosa counters; a Nairobi afternoon ritual.

places.name: Nairobi Java House
places.note: Home-grown chain, dependable for chai and Kenyan coffee if street stalls feel daunting.

places.name: City Market
places.note: Vendors pouring hot chai from flasks for market traders through the morning.

food.name: Tusker lager
food.desc: Kenya's flagship beer since 1922, drunk cold with grilled meat. Ask for it baridi for chilled or the local habit of room temperature.

places.name: Brew Bistro
places.note: Nairobi craft-brewing pioneer; good for local beers beyond the mainstream lagers.

places.name: The Alchemist
places.note: Open-air yard with food trucks and live music, a fixture of the Westlands night scene.

places.name: Carnivore Restaurant
places.note: Cold Tusker with nyama choma is the classic Nairobi pairing; also home to the Simba Saloon.

landmarks: Nairobi National Park
The only national park bordering a capital city in the world, offering photos of lions, rhinos, and giraffes with the Nairobi skyline as a backdrop.
Giraffe Centre
A beloved conservation spot where visitors hand-feed endangered Rothschild's giraffes at eye level from an elevated platform.
David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust
Home to the world's most successful orphaned elephant rescue and rehabilitation program, famous for its adorable baby-elephant feeding sessions.
Karen Blixen Museum
The restored colonial farmhouse of "Out of Africa" author Karen Blixen, set against the Ngong Hills and steeped in early-20th-century Kenyan history.
Nairobi National Museum
Kenya's premier museum showcasing the country's rich paleontological, cultural, and artistic heritage, including early hominid fossils.
Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC)
Nairobi's iconic cylindrical tower, an architectural symbol of the city offering sweeping 360-degree rooftop views.
Bomas of Kenya
A lively cultural village celebrating Kenya's many ethnic traditions through recreated homesteads and vibrant traditional dance performances.
Nairobi Railway Museum
A nostalgic collection of vintage steam locomotives and carriages tracing the storied history of the Uganda Railway, the "Lunatic Express."
Uhuru Gardens National Monument
The historic site where Kenya's flag was first raised at independence in 1963, marked by a striking monument and museum.
Karura Forest
A 1,000-hectare urban forest on Nairobi's northern edge with waterfalls, caves, and trails for walking and cycling among monkeys and birdlife.

train.note: No international passenger train. The Madaraka Express standard-gauge (SGR) service runs daytime from Nairobi Terminus (Syokimau) to Mombasa, with intermediate stops and a branch to Naivasha/Suswa; book online at metickets.krc.co.ke or the M-Pesa line. Bring ID/passport - it is checked at the station.

intl.to: Kampala (Uganda), Kigali (Rwanda), Dar es Salaam (Tanzania), Bujumbura (Burundi) & Juba (South Sudan)
Kampala (Uganda) & Dar es Salaam (Tanzania) via Arusha

bus.note: Cross-border coaches leave from the operators' terminals around the Accra Road / River Road area of central Nairobi, mostly on overnight departures. Carry your passport - visas/border stops apply for Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi and South Sudan.

ferry.note: Nairobi is inland with no ferries. Passenger boats operate elsewhere in Kenya - on Lake Victoria (Kisumu) and along the coast around Mombasa/Lamu.

half.name: Hell's Gate National Park
half.blurb: Cycle or walk among towering gorges and cliffs where wildlife roams freely.

half.name: Lake Naivasha
half.blurb: A freshwater lake famed for hippos, birdlife and scenic boat rides.

half.name: Mount Longonot
half.blurb: Hike this dormant volcano's crater rim for sweeping Rift Valley panoramas.

half.name: Ngong Hills
half.blurb: Green ridgeline hikes offer breezy views over the Rift Valley and city.

half.name: Lake Magadi
half.blurb: A striking pink soda lake in dry country, dotted with flamingos and hot springs.

full.name: Lake Nakuru National Park
full.blurb: Flamingo-lined shores and rhinos make this lake park a beloved safari destination.
